Appendix A Experimental details and reproducibility

This appendix documents per-experiment hyperparameters, extended tables, and reproducibility notes for each empirical claim, organised as follows.

Theory and scope (§A.1–§A.3). The theory-to-scope map gives per-prediction assumption sets, validation loci, and explicit failure conditions; the key-results sketch (§A.2) restates the four framework results used in the body in compact equation-level form with 11–33 line proof sketches (LN-kernel direction, RMSNorm differential, σmin\sigma_{\min} depth-invariance, Schur-ratio prefactor), so a reader can verify the empirical claims against an explicit derivation without opening the theory paper; framing-only predictions (composition additivity, quotient Fisher rate) are stated for reference.

Measurement protocols (§A.4). Per-observable computation recipes for the activation-side measurements this paper uses: residual-stream σmin\sigma_{\min} via fp6464 centred-cov SVD, the Schur-ratio R⁡(h)R(h) probe along the framework-predicted direction u=γ−1/‖γ−1‖u=\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\|, chunked-covariance accumulation at LLM widths, fp6464 upcast for the massive-activations regime (σmax≳105\sigma_{\max}\gtrsim 10^{5}), and n/hn/h sample-budget gates.

LLM-scale fingerprint and diagnosis (§A.5, §A.6). Supports the body’s LLM-scale results: per-model residual-stream fingerprint table on the 1414-model set; Pythia-1B pretraining-revision developmental arc; ViT FFN fine-tuning trajectory test; the five-mechanism Gemma 44 anomaly diagnosis.

Cross-architecture feasibility and compute (§A.7–§A.8). Tractability across the architecture set, hardware envelope, and reproducibility notes.

A.1 Theory-to-scope map

The body’s §4 opening paragraph names every load-bearing prediction with its class and validation locus. The reach-tier roll-up below is the same information at one level of abstraction higher: each row is a class of prediction with a single representative theorem; “Off-the-shelf testable” indicates whether the prediction can be validated on a frozen pretrained transformer with no gradient access.

Reach tier Representative prediction Where validated Off-the-shelf?
Architecture-agnostic structural σmin\sigma_{\min} depth-invariance (Cor. 4) on residual DAGs with exact-identity skips 1414 pretrained transformers under fp6464 centred-cov measurement (§4); 13/1413/14 pass on each model’s own input distribution, the one exception Gemma4-31B (intrinsic near-dead direction); Gemma4-E4B’s text-only dip resolves as distribution-relative Yes
Norm-side algebraic LN-kernel γ−1/‖γ−1‖\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\| (Prop. 2); RMSNorm differential (Prop. 3) 1414 pretrained transformers (§4); Schur-ratio cross-model sweep Yes

Both reach tiers tested in this paper are off-the-shelf: every result above is read from a frozen pretrained transformer with no gradient access and no SGLD chain. The framework’s wider rate-side predictions (Fisher decay Θ⁡(t2​(k−1))\Theta(t^{2(k-1)}), selection rule, multi-layer KFAC bridge per-layer rate ladder 2​(L−ℓ)/ℓ2(L-\ell)/\ell, curvature–volume rate chain) require a controlled SGD-class trajectory and are not validated here.

All 1414 pretrained transformers in our set use exact-identity residual streams (no gated or highway residuals); the MoE in Qwen3.6-35B-A3B applies routing only to the FFN sub-block, not to the residual skip itself, so Corollary 58’s exact-identity-skip hypothesis applies.

A.2 Key results from the framework, with proof sketches

The empirical claims rest on four results of Shirodkar (2026). We restate each in compact form with a 2–3 line proof sketch; full proofs (with all assumptions, supporting lemmas, and architectural extensions) live in the theory paper. Throughout, LN⁡(x)=γ⊙x~LN​(x)+β\mathrm{LN}(x)=\gamma\odot\tilde{x}_{\mathrm{LN}}(x)+\beta with x~LN​(x)=d​P​x/‖P​x‖\tilde{x}_{\mathrm{LN}}(x)=\sqrt{d}\,Px/\|Px\| and P:=I−𝟏d​𝟏d⊤/dP:=I-\mathbf{1}_{d}\mathbf{1}_{d}^{\top}/d the mean-subtraction projector; RMSNorm⁡(x)=γ⊙x/‖x‖2/d\mathrm{RMSNorm}(x)=\gamma\odot x/\sqrt{\|x\|^{2}/d} has no projector. Xℓ∈ℝN×hX_{\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times h} stacks per-token residual-stream activations at block ℓ\ell; Aℓ:=𝔼⁡[Xℓ−1​Xℓ−1⊤]A_{\ell}:=\mathbb{E}[X_{\ell-1}X_{\ell-1}^{\top}] is the input covariance at layer ℓ\ell.

P1. LN-kernel direction (Prop. 63, theory paper).

For any input XX with P​X≠0PX\neq 0 a.s. (i.e., not concentrated on the constant-vector line span⁡(𝟏d)\mathrm{span}(\mathbf{1}_{d})) and γ\gamma with γi≠0\gamma_{i}\neq 0 for all ii:

cov⁡(LN⁡(X))⋅γ−1= 0,kernel direction ​v⋆=γ−1/‖γ−1‖.\mathrm{cov}(\mathrm{LN}(X))\cdot\gamma^{-1}\;=\;0,\qquad\text{kernel direction }v^{\star}\;=\;\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\|.

Sketch (3 lines). (a) 𝟏d⊤​x~LN​(X)=d​ 1d⊤​P​X/‖P​X‖=0\mathbf{1}_{d}^{\top}\tilde{x}_{\mathrm{LN}}(X)=\sqrt{d}\,\mathbf{1}_{d}^{\top}PX/\|PX\|=0 a.s. since 𝟏d⊤​P=0\mathbf{1}_{d}^{\top}P=0. (b) Hence cov⁡(x~LN)​𝟏d=𝔼⁡[x~LN​(𝟏d⊤​x~LN)]=0\mathrm{cov}(\tilde{x}_{\mathrm{LN}})\mathbf{1}_{d}=\mathbb{E}[\tilde{x}_{\mathrm{LN}}(\mathbf{1}_{d}^{\top}\tilde{x}_{\mathrm{LN}})]=0. (c) With LN⁡(X)=diag⁡(γ)​x~LN+β\mathrm{LN}(X)=\mathrm{diag}(\gamma)\tilde{x}_{\mathrm{LN}}+\beta and β\beta contributing nothing to covariance, cov⁡(LN⁡(X))​γ−1=diag⁡(γ)​cov​(x~LN)​diag​(γ)​γ−1=diag⁡(γ)​cov​(x~LN)​ 1d=0\mathrm{cov}(\mathrm{LN}(X))\gamma^{-1}=\mathrm{diag}(\gamma)\,\mathrm{cov}(\tilde{x}_{\mathrm{LN}})\,\mathrm{diag}(\gamma)\,\gamma^{-1}=\mathrm{diag}(\gamma)\,\mathrm{cov}(\tilde{x}_{\mathrm{LN}})\,\mathbf{1}_{d}=0. The unit kernel direction v⋆v^{\star} is read from the LN affine alone, no forward pass required.

P2. RMSNorm differential (Prop. 63, theory paper).

For γ\gamma with γi≠0\gamma_{i}\neq 0 for all ii, no unit direction v⁡(γ)v(\gamma) depending only on γ\gamma universally satisfies v⊤​cov​(RMSNorm⁡(X))​v=0v^{\top}\mathrm{cov}(\mathrm{RMSNorm}(X))v=0 across all input distributions with cov⁡(X)≻0\mathrm{cov}(X)\succ 0. Sketch (1 line). Take X∼𝒩⁡(0,Id)X\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d}): r⁡(X)​X=d​X/‖X‖r(X)X=\sqrt{d}\,X/\|X\| is uniform on d​Sd−1\sqrt{d}\,S^{d-1}, with cov=Id\mathrm{cov}=I_{d} by spherical symmetry; hence ‖γ⊙v‖2>0\|\gamma\odot v\|^{2}>0 for any v≠0v\neq 0, contradicting universality. The structural distinction is the absence of the mean-subtraction projector PP: RMSNorm’s x~RMS\tilde{x}_{\mathrm{RMS}} does not live in 𝟏d⟂\mathbf{1}_{d}^{\perp}, so no kernel direction is forced by γ\gamma alone.

C3. σmin\sigma_{\min} depth-invariance on residual DAGs (Cor. 58, theory paper).

For a residual DAG with exact-identity skips and arbitrary residual-branch contributions Δℓ\Delta_{\ell}, Xℓ+1=Xℓ+Δℓ​(Xℓ)X_{\ell+1}=X_{\ell}+\Delta_{\ell}(X_{\ell}). Then under generic non-cancellation between XℓX_{\ell} and Δℓ\Delta_{\ell}:

σ(r0)​(Xℓ+1)≥σ(r0)​(Xℓ),equivalently ​σ(r0)​(Xℓ)/σ(r0)​(X0)≥1​ for all ​ℓ.\sigma_{(r_{0})}(X_{\ell+1})\;\geq\;\sigma_{(r_{0})}(X_{\ell}),\qquad\text{equivalently }\sigma_{(r_{0})}(X_{\ell})/\sigma_{(r_{0})}(X_{0})\geq 1\text{ for all }\ell.

Sketch (2 lines). The r0r_{0}-th singular value of a sum is bounded below by the corresponding singular value of any term minus the cancellation between terms. Identity-skip means the column space of XℓX_{\ell} embeds into Xℓ+1X_{\ell+1}, so without exact destructive interference the bottom of the active spectrum either stays put or grows. The corollary’s failure mode is precisely cancellation: Δℓ​(Xℓ)≈−Xℓ+noise\Delta_{\ell}(X_{\ell})\approx-X_{\ell}+\text{noise} at some block (the empirical Gemma 44 failure, App. A.6).

L4. Schur-ratio quantitative prefactor (Lem. 18, theory paper).

At a Type-A site (Linear layer fed by a LayerNorm output), with u⋆:=γ−1/‖γ−1‖u^{\star}:=\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\| the predicted dead direction:

R⁡(h):=λmin​(Aℓ)(Aℓ)u⋆,u⋆→N→∞ 1,finite-​N​ drift ∼ 2​h/N−h/N​ (Marchenko–Pastur).R(h)\;:=\;\frac{\lambda_{\min}(A_{\ell})}{(A_{\ell})_{u^{\star},u^{\star}}}\;\xrightarrow{N\to\infty}\;1,\qquad\text{finite-}N\text{ drift }\;\sim\;2\sqrt{h/N}-h/N\text{ (Marchenko--Pastur)}.

Sketch (3 lines). The asymptotic limit is a direct consequence of P1: in the population, u⋆u^{\star} is exactly arg⁡minv​v⊤​Aℓ​v\arg\min_{v}v^{\top}A_{\ell}v (kernel direction of the post-LN cov), so the numerator and denominator coincide. At finite NN, the empirical λmin\lambda_{\min} is biased downward by the bottom of the Marchenko–Pastur band ∼(1−h/N)2\sim(1-\sqrt{h/N})^{2}, while (Aℓ)u⋆,u⋆(A_{\ell})_{u^{\star},u^{\star}} at the population direction is unbiased; their ratio tracks the MP correction. The closed-form constant c=(h−1)/(π⁡(π+h−2))c=(h-1)/(\pi(\pi+h-2)) for the Schur complement at the Type-A site (Lemma 5 of §3) sets the leading-NN prefactor; we use the MP drift band as the data-side baseline against which the trained-checkpoint Δγ→1\Delta_{\gamma}\to 1 is read.

Reading the empirical observables.

|cos⁡(u⊥,v⋆)||\cos(u_{\bot},v^{\star})|: principal-angle alignment of the measured bottom singular direction u⊥u_{\bot} of the post-final-LN centred covariance with the framework-predicted v⋆=γ−1/‖γ−1‖v^{\star}=\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\| read from the LN affine. P1 predicts |cos|=1|\cos|=1 exactly in the population; finite-NN measurement at fp6464 centred-cov gives ≥0.9999\geq 0.9999 on every LN model in the set.
Δγ:=1−R⁡(h)\Delta_{\gamma}:=1-R(h): the gap between the actual bottom of the per-block input covariance and the eigenvalue along the predicted direction u⋆u^{\star}. Δγ≈0\Delta_{\gamma}\approx 0 means the predicted direction is exactly the bottom; Δγ≈1\Delta_{\gamma}\approx 1 means training has opened a deeper dead direction along some other coordinate.
σmin​(Xℓ)/σmin​(X0)\sigma_{\min}(X_{\ell})/\sigma_{\min}(X_{0}): residual-stream ratio tested by C3 (≥1\geq 1 at every block on 13/1413/14 pretrained transformers read on each model’s own input distribution; the one exception Gemma4-31B is a genuine intrinsic dead direction, Gemma4-E4B’s text-only dip distribution-relative).

The 1414-model fingerprint validates P1 (LN models, |cos|≥0.9999|\cos|\geq 0.9999 on 9/99/9), P2 (RMSNorm models, |cos|≤0.10|\cos|\leq 0.10 on 5/55/5), C3 (13/1413/14 pass on each model’s own input distribution; the one Gemma4-31B exception characterised by family ablation and multimodal recalibration), and L4 (Δγ\Delta_{\gamma} within finite-NN MP band at random init, saturating at ≈1\approx 1 on the trained checkpoint with a 33–18×18\times directional beat over the axis-aligned default).

A.3 Framing-only predictions used in the discussion

The two predictions below are referenced in the body but not directly tested in the empirical experiments of §4. They are restated here for completeness; the full assumption sets, proofs, and architectural extensions are in Shirodkar (2026).

Theorem 6 (Composition additivity; Shirodkar, 2026, Thm. 30).

For a sequential stack of MLP / pre-norm residual blocks with shared dead direction, the dead-direction Fisher rate at the input of block BiB_{i} is Θ⁡(t2​∑j≥ikjbk)\Theta(t^{2\sum_{j\geq i}k_{j}^{\mathrm{bk}}}): per-block backward rates kjbkk_{j}^{\mathrm{bk}} add along the path. Pure attention chains at depth ≥4\geq 4 break this additivity via softmax cross-block coupling (Remark 32); the closed-form refinement at the per-component level is Prop. 69 of Shirodkar (2026). This theorem is the basis for the architectural extensions to rectangular widths, biases, cross-entropy with Z-loss gauge fix, and the residual-DAG / attention-chain composition results referenced as scope statements throughout §4.

Corollary 7 (Quotient Fisher rate; Shirodkar, 2026, Cor. 78).

For losses invariant under a continuous Lie group GG acting on Θ\Theta, Theorem 2’s rate identity holds verbatim on the gauge quotient Θ/G\Theta/G, with the gauge orbit playing the role of a smooth singular fibre. Projected SGD on Θ/G\Theta/G realises the quotient rate (Cor. 79). Adam’s per-coordinate preconditioner is not GG-equivariant: its trajectory carries gauge-mode drift and the trajectory-rate readout is not directly applicable to Adam-class dynamics (Remark 80). This corollary scopes the trajectory-rate-readout claims of the framework, which are out-of-scope for this paper.

A.4 Observable computation protocols

The LN-kernel diagnostic, the residual-stream σmin\sigma_{\min} depth-invariance test, and the Schur-ratio quantitative prefactor all read from a single forward pass on calibration data per checkpoint. No backward pass, no SGLD chain, no gradient capture.

σmin​(Xℓ)\sigma_{\min}(X_{\ell}) on activations (real-time cadence).

For each transformer block ℓ\ell, capture the residual-stream activation matrix Xℓ∈ℝN×hX_{\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times h} in a single forward pass over NN calibration tokens (we use N=8192N=8192 at LLM scale via WikiText calibration; ImageNet validation for ViTs). For widths h>4096h>4096 (Qwen3.6-2727B at h=5120h{=}5120, Gemma4-3131B at h=5376h{=}5376) use chunked covariance accumulation Cℓ=∑chunksXℓ⊤​XℓC_{\ell}=\sum_{\mathrm{chunks}}X_{\ell}^{\top}X_{\ell} and eigendecompose CℓC_{\ell} to recover the singular values; this keeps peak memory bounded on a single 3090. Cost: 1 forward pass per checkpoint, all layers (the per-layer SVD is post-hoc on the captured activations).

Centred-covariance protocol.

The LN-kernel prediction (Prop. 2) is for the post-norm centred activation covariance Cov⁡(LN⁡(X))=𝔼⁡[(LN⁡(X)−𝔼⁡[LN⁡(X)])​(⋅)⊤]\cov(\mathrm{LN}(X))=\mathbb{E}[(\mathrm{LN}(X)-\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{LN}(X)])(\cdot)^{\top}], which projects out LN’s mean-centring direction 𝟏d\mathbf{1}_{d}. Reading the bottom direction off the raw Gram X⊤​XX^{\top}X instead conflates the γ−1\gamma^{-1} kernel with the 𝟏d\mathbf{1}_{d} projector. We accumulate the centred covariance directly: subtract the per-token mean before forming the chunked sum, eigendecompose at fp6464, report the bottom singular direction u⊥u_{\bot}. The centred protocol is mandatory whenever |cos⁡(β,γ−1)|>0.1|\cos(\beta,\gamma^{-1})|>0.1 (every LN model in our set passes this guard); raw-Gram values are reported alongside as a sanity contrast.

fp-precision recipe at the bottom of the spectrum.

Default cov accumulation is fp3232 on a single 3090. For inputs with σmax≳105\sigma_{\max}\gtrsim 10^{5} (the massive-activations regime), the fp3232 noise floor σmax​εfp32\sigma_{\max}\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fp32}}} sits above the bottom of the active spectrum and the input reads as if numerically rank-deficient. fp6464 cov drops the floor by ∼8\sim 8 OOM at ∼2×\sim 2\times memory and ∼2×\sim 2\times GEMM cost; the σmax\sigma_{\max} scale itself is the cheap pre-flight check. We use fp6464 cov on every model with σmax≳105\sigma_{\max}\gtrsim 10^{5} (DINOv33-ViT-L, Qwen3.53.5-44B, Gemma44-3131B) and fp3232 on the rest; both modes log the cov dtype in run JSON. The eigendecomposition is fp6464 in both cases.

Sample-budget gate.

Stable estimation of the smallest active eigenvalue requires n/h≥100n/h\geq 100 tokens per hidden dimension; smaller nn gives CV >100%>100\% on magnitude estimates. At h≤5376h\leq 5376 (every model in our set) the default N=8192N{=}8192 tokens give n/h≥1.5n/h\geq 1.5 on the worst case before chunking; chunked accumulation across a 32,76832{,}768-token batch lifts the effective n/hn/h to ≥6\geq 6 on every model. For bottom-of-spectrum reads at depth, the analytical CV bound from first-order perturbation theory + Davis–Kahan is CV⁡(λmin+)≤(1/N)⋅(σmax/σmin)\mathrm{CV}(\lambda_{\min}^{+})\leq(1/\sqrt{N})\cdot(\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}), typically 55–10×10\times pessimistic on structured covariances, much tighter than the operator-norm Wishart bound D/N⋅(σmax/σmin)2\sqrt{D/N}\cdot(\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min})^{2} which is 5050–500×500\times pessimistic on the same data.

Schur-ratio measurement.

The Schur ratio R⁡(h):=λmin​(Aℓ)/(Aℓ)u,uR(h):=\lambda_{\min}(A_{\ell})/(A_{\ell})_{u,u} at the predicted direction u=γ−1/‖γ−1‖u=\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\| uses the same chunked-covariance accumulator: form the per-block AℓA_{\ell} (input activation Gram), compute λmin​(Aℓ)\lambda_{\min}(A_{\ell}) from its fp6464 eigendecomposition, and extract the diagonal element (Aℓ)u,u=u⊤​Aℓ​u(A_{\ell})_{u,u}=u^{\top}A_{\ell}u along the framework-predicted direction in the same step. The complement Δγ:=1−R⁡(h)\Delta_{\gamma}:=1-R(h) is the depth of the dead channel; protocol details and per-block-type measurement sites (qkv input, mlp.up input, mlp.down input, o-proj input) are in App. A.6.

A.5 LLM scale-pipeline (§4)

Per-model fingerprint.

Table 2 gives the depth-profile statistics referenced in the main body. Each row is one forward pass per layer per checkpoint. The behaviour column classifies each model by whether the body residual-stream σmin\sigma_{\min} trajectory satisfies Corollary 58’s strict prediction (depth-invariant, ratio ≥1\geq 1 at every block) or shows residual-branch non-cancellation (intermediate-dip for transient sub-11 ratios that recover by the output, depth-decreasing for profiles whose output σmin\sigma_{\min} ends below the input). All σmin\sigma_{\min} values are reported under the fp6464 centered-covariance protocol (--cov-dtype float64); the well-conditioned majority of models with σmax≲103\sigma_{\max}\lesssim 10^{3} have fp3232- and fp6464-cov readings agreeing to fingerprint precision, but the inputs of DINOv3-ViT-L (σmax≈106\sigma_{\max}\approx 10^{6}) and several other models read as σmin​(X0)=0\sigma_{\min}(X_{0})=0 under fp3232 cov from the σmax⋅εfp32\sigma_{\max}\cdot\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fp}32}} accumulator floor; fp6464 cov resolves the active spectrum, and the ratio test uses the rank-aware smallest active singular value σ(r0)\sigma_{(r_{0})} against X0X_{0} (DINOv3-ViT-L’s embedding is additionally rank-deficient, r0=947/1024r_{0}=947/1024, so its σmin​(X0)=0\sigma_{\min}(X_{0})=0 is structural and the σ(r0)\sigma_{(r_{0})} reference is the operative one). The two cosine columns report the post-final-normalization-hook alignment of the bottom singular direction with the uniform-γ\gamma reference 𝟏d/d\mathbf{1}_{d}/\sqrt{d} and with the exact Proposition 63 direction γ−1/‖γ−1‖\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\| read from the terminal normalization’s learned affine (the zero-γ\gamma-coordinate limit is the coordinate-indicator vector).

Models and provenance.

Pythia-160M, Pythia-1B (Biderman et al., 2023); Qwen3.5-4B (Team, 2026b); Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Team, 2026c); Gemma4-E4B, Gemma4-31B (Team, 2026a); DINOv3-ViT-S/L (Siméoni et al., 2025), DINOv2-base (Oquab et al., 2023), ViT-B/16 (Dosovitskiy et al., 2021), ViT-MAE-base (He et al., 2022), SigLIP2-base (Tschannen et al., 2025), V-JEPA 2 ViT-L (Assran et al., 2025). All via HuggingFace Hub or timm.

Calibration corpus.

For language models, WikiText-103 validation split, 3232 sequences of 256256 tokens (N=8192N=8192 per layer, comfortably above hh for all models in the table). For vision models, 3232 ImageNet validation images preprocessed through each model’s published image-processor; the centered-covariance LN-kernel prediction is provably input-distribution-invariant (|Δ​cos|<10−6|\Delta\cos|<10^{-6} between synthetic-noise and ImageNet calibration on all 55 standard ViTs in the set), so synthetic-noise calibration is a defensible cheap variant for fingerprinting on the centered protocol, we report ImageNet numbers as primary because the reviewer-facing input distribution should be a real one.

σmin\sigma_{\min} computation protocol (centered covariance).

For each block ℓ\ell, mean-center the residual-stream activations across the NN calibration samples and accumulate the covariance Cℓ=(1/N)∑i,t(Xℓ[i,t,:]−X¯ℓ)(Xℓ[i,t,:]−X¯ℓ)⊤C_{\ell}=(1/N)\sum_{i,t}(X_{\ell}[i,t,:]-\bar{X}_{\ell})(X_{\ell}[i,t,:]-\bar{X}_{\ell})^{\top} in chunked fp32, then SVD in fp64. The centered protocol is what Proposition 63 actually predicts and is the empirical primary throughout. We additionally report the raw-Gram ∑i,tXℓ​Xℓ⊤\sum_{i,t}X_{\ell}X_{\ell}^{\top} protocol as a check: on 13/1413/14 models the LN bias β\beta has |cos⁡(β,γ−1)|≤0.05|\cos(\beta,\gamma^{-1})|\leq 0.05 and the two protocols agree to |Δ​cos|<0.02|\Delta\cos|<0.02 on the post-final-norm cosine; vit-base has |cos⁡(β,γ−1)|=0.24|\cos(\beta,\gamma^{-1})|=0.24 and the protocols differ (0.540.54 raw, 1.0001.000 centered), illustrating exactly why Proposition 63’s centered statement is the empirically correct one. The post-final-normalization hook (indexed as layer LL) is the position at which the algebraic-kernel prediction is read on LN-based architectures. Wall times per full fingerprint: <1<1 s at Pythia-160M; 33 s at Pythia-1B; 1111 s at Qwen3.5-4B; 1313 s at Gemma4-E4B; <1<1 s at each vision transformer. The released code emits both raw-Gram and centered SVDs in the same per-run JSON.

Measurement precision: fp64 covariance accumulation.

The σ\sigma-based test of Corollary 58 is sensitive to the covariance accumulator’s precision. With fp3232 accumulation (the published protocol on most fingerprint-style observables), σ\sigma values below σmax​(Xℓ)⋅εfp32≈σmax⋅3×10−4\sigma_{\max}(X_{\ell})\cdot\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fp}32}}\approx\sigma_{\max}\cdot 3\times 10^{-4} are absorbed into accumulator noise regardless of downstream SVD precision. For inputs with σmax≳105\sigma_{\max}\gtrsim 10^{5} (the documented massive-activations regime, Sun et al. (2024); related to the low-effective-rank class structure of deep-learning spectra, Papyan (2020)), this places the noise floor above the bottom of the active spectrum and the strict ratio test reads as if X0X_{0} had a numerical-zero kernel. We report σmin\sigma_{\min} measurements at fp6464 accumulation, which extends the noise floor to σmax⋅εfp64≈σmax⋅1.5×10−8\sigma_{\max}\cdot\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fp}64}}\approx\sigma_{\max}\cdot 1.5\times 10^{-8}, eight orders of magnitude lower, at 2×2\times accumulator memory and roughly 2×2\times GEMM cost (a few seconds longer at fingerprint scale, 55–1010 minutes longer on 3030B-class models with CPU offload). fp3232 cov remains a sensible back-compat default and is sufficient for inputs with σmax≲103\sigma_{\max}\lesssim 10^{3}; fp6464 is the recommended protocol whenever the input residual stream is in the massive-activations regime, with the σmax\sigma_{\max} scale itself a cheap pre-flight check. Covariance precision is necessary but not sufficient: the forward-pass capture dtype imposes an independent floor. The two highest-σmax\sigma_{\max} RMSNorm models (Qwen3.6-27B, Gemma4-31B, σmax≈1.6×104\sigma_{\max}\approx 1.6\times 10^{4} centered) read a spurious σmin=0\sigma_{\min}=0 at every block under bf1616 forward even with fp6464 cov; fp3232 forward at n/d≥10n/d\geq 10 resolves both to full numerical rank (the vision transformers already capture in fp3232, so DINOv3-ViT-L at σmax≈106\sigma_{\max}\approx 10^{6} needed only the fp6464-cov fix). With fp3232 forward and fp6464 cov, every model’s block outputs X1,…,XLX_{1},\ldots,X_{L} have σ(r0)=σmin\sigma_{(r_{0})}=\sigma_{\min} at full rank, so on the body the rank-aware Corollary 58 and the strict ratio σmin​(Xℓ)/σmin​(X0)\sigma_{\min}(X_{\ell})/\sigma_{\min}(X_{0}) coincide. The one place they differ is DINOv3-ViT-L’s input embedding (r0=947/1024r_{0}=947/1024, σmin​(X0)=0\sigma_{\min}(X_{0})=0), where the rank-aware σ(r0)​(X0)\sigma_{(r_{0})}(X_{0}) is the operative reference; we report the rank-aware ratio there and the coincident strict ratio elsewhere. The n/dn/d column governs the precision of the absolute σmin\sigma_{\min} magnitudes (biased low below n/d≈10n/d\approx 10, hence reported as architectural baselines); the ratio test itself is n/dn/d-robust.

What the LLM-scale test actually measures.

The strict statement σmin​(Xℓ)/σmin​(X0)≥1\sigma_{\min}(X_{\ell})/\sigma_{\min}(X_{0})\geq 1 is a path-decomposition consequence of identity skips wherever the no-cancellation hypothesis (Remark 59) holds at the bottom-of-active-spectrum direction. As a pass/fail count alone, 12/1412/14 is therefore a relatively soft test of the corollary, the same prediction holds at random initialisation on 5/55/5 architectures (§“Trained vs random-init baseline” below; the architectural-vs-training distinction is also developed in Shirodkar, 2026). The non-trivial empirical content of the trained-network fingerprint is the failures: the Gemma 44 release (both checkpoints) localises the no-cancellation hypothesis as failable, with the failure modes diagnostically traceable to specific block ranges.

Falsifications of the trained-network no-cancellation hypothesis.

The two Gemma 44 releases violate the strict prediction under the resolved protocol (fp6464 cov, n/d≥10n/d\geq 10, fp3232 forward, referenced against the true input embedding X0X_{0}):

  • •

    Gemma4-31B (depth-decreasing). The body σmin\sigma_{\min} profile is non-monotone: an early dip, a mid-depth recovery to ∼3.9×\sim 3.9\times, then a declining tail to ∼0.05\sim 0.05 of the input at the output (37/6037/60 body blocks below X0X_{0}, output ratio 0.0540.054, a net ∼18×\sim 18\times reduction; min ratio 0.0320.032 at block 5353). The residual stream fails to preserve σmin\sigma_{\min}; the Gemma 44 release is the outlier in our set (the smaller Gemma 44-E44B at the same release fails too) and is empirically dissociated from the Peri-LN sandwich-norm pattern (§A.6). Under bf1616 forward this profile floors to a spurious σmin=0\sigma_{\min}=0 at every block; the finite reduction is the fp3232-forward reading.

  • •

    Gemma4-E4B (intermediate-depth dip). Min ratio 0.0310.031 at block 2323 of 4242 (24/4224/42 body blocks below X0X_{0}), recovering to ∼1.1×\sim 1.1\times at the output.

The Gemma 44 failures are the strongest empirical signal in the LLM-scale fingerprint: they identify a per-checkpoint violation of an assumption the corollary makes explicit, at specific block ranges, on a published frontier model family. A family discriminator across Gemma 11 through Gemma 44 (§A.6) dissociates the failure from the normalisation placement: pre-LN Gemma 11 (22b, 77b) and Peri-LN (Kim et al., 2025) Gemma 22-22b, Gemma 33-11b/44b/1212b all preserve σmin\sigma_{\min} against X0X_{0} (min ratio ≥1.8\geq 1.8, output 9.99.9–632×632\times), and only the Gemma 44 release, which shares the Peri-LN pattern, fails. A five-mechanism ablation tests γpost\gamma_{\mathrm{post}}-kernel formation, per-block residual-vs-delta cancellation, the sandwich-norm pattern itself, centred-cov sink-token bias, and post-pretraining stage, and rules each out individually; the σmin\sigma_{\min} collapse localises to the MLP sub-layer, where the drops concentrate (28/4228/42 blocks on E4B, 40/6040/60 on 31B, against 22 and 66 on attention) under an effective-rank collapse at the minimum-ratio block. The cause within the Gemma 44 release is partly resolved: multimodal recalibration traces Gemma4-E4B’s text-only dip to a dormant-modality calibration effect (a distribution-relative dead direction that dissolves under its full text++image++audio distribution), while Gemma4-31B retains a genuine intrinsic near-dead direction above the fp3232 measurement floor; the training-recipe difference from the earlier releases that would explain Gemma4-31B’s residual direction remains an open follow-up.

Passing models and architectural baseline.

The remaining 1212 architectures pass at every block, with per-model passing ratios from 1.01.0 at X0X_{0} to several-hundred-fold at the deepest blocks (Qwen3.6-27B reaches 651×651\times; per-model magnitudes are not predicted by Corollary 58, only the rate-00 statement is; magnitudes are reported as architectural baselines for the amplification analysis below, and below n/d≈10n/d\approx 10 they are biased low by the Marchenko–Pastur edge). Several apparent “failures” resolved once the measurement and the reference were adequate. Referencing against the true input embedding X0X_{0} (the block-00 output is X1X_{1}, one residual node past the embedding) turns DINOv3-ViT-S/1616 (min ratio 1.2×1.2\times at block 33, 3.4×3.4\times at the output) and SigLIP2-base (min 20×20\times at block 66, 101×101\times at the output) into clean passes; both dip below 11 only against the block-00 output, never against X0X_{0}. DINOv3-ViT-L (fp3232 forward, σmax≈106\sigma_{\max}\approx 10^{6}, rank-deficient embedding r0=947/1024r_{0}=947/1024) reads σmin​(X0)=0\sigma_{\min}(X_{0})=0; fp6464 cov resolves its active spectrum and the rank-aware σ(r0)\sigma_{(r_{0})} ratio passes 24/2424/24 with wide margin. Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma4-31B read a spurious σmin=0\sigma_{\min}=0 at every block under bf1616 forward (the capture floor sits above the active bottom regardless of cov precision); fp3232 forward at n/d≥10n/d\geq 10 resolves Qwen3.6-27B to a clean 64/6464/64 pass (0.52→121×0.52\to 121\times) and Gemma4-31B to the finite depth-decreasing profile above.

The pretrained-fingerprint and pretraining-trajectory experiments in this section (Pythia-1B revisions, ViT FFN fine-tuning) live in the well-conditioned regime (σmax∼102\sigma_{\max}\sim 10^{2}) where fp3232 and fp6464 cov agree to fingerprint precision; their published numbers are not affected by the precision-protocol distinction. The released code reports σmin\sigma_{\min}, σ(r0)\sigma_{(r_{0})}, and the active-rank index per block at the chosen cov precision; downstream analysis routes on the cov-precision field surfaced in the per-run JSON metadata block.

Trained vs random-init baseline.

The strict prediction σmin​(Xℓ)/σmin​(X0)≥1\sigma_{\min}(X_{\ell})/\sigma_{\min}(X_{0})\geq 1 of Corollary 58 is satisfied by the additive-identity skip structure at any θ\theta for which the no-cancellation hypothesis (Remark 59) holds, including random initialisation. To make this explicit at LLM scale, we re-run the same fp6464 centered-cov pipeline on a fresh config-only re-init of each model under HuggingFace’s default _init_weights schemes (torch.manual_seed(42), AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(cfg) for LLMs / AutoModel.from_config(cfg) for ViTs) and compare against the trained checkpoint at the same calibration corpus and n/dn/d:

Model LL Norm trained max rℓr_{\ell} randinit max rℓr_{\ell} trained post-LN randinit post-LN
Pythia-160M 1212 LN 19.6919.69 2.692.69 2.952.95 0.060.06
Pythia-1B 1616 LN 64.9564.95 7.557.55 — —
Qwen3.5-4B 3232 RMSNorm 84.6384.63 7.477.47 1.001.00 0.060.06
DINOv2-base 1212 LN 7.927.92 2.222.22 1.001.00 0.210.21
ViT-MAE-base 1212 LN 3.533.53 1.941.94 — —

The rate-00 statement rℓ≥1r_{\ell}\geq 1 holds at every body block on 5/55/5 architectures at random initialisation, so the pass/fail of the strict prediction does not by itself discriminate trained from random networks. What the trained-vs-randinit comparison does surface is the amplification gap, the dynamics signal training adds on top of the architectural baseline. Trained max ratios range 3.5×3.5\times–84.6×84.6\times vs random-init 1.9×1.9\times–7.5×7.5\times (a 33–11×11\times multiplicative amplification across architectures); the post-final-normalisation ratio gap is sharper still (∼50×\sim\!50\times on Pythia-160M, ∼17×\sim\!17\times on Qwen3.5-4B, ∼5×\sim\!5\times on DINOv2-base). The Pythia-1B step1 HuggingFace revision (network after one optimiser step on real data) reads max rℓ=16.39r_{\ell}=16.39, sitting between trained (64.9564.95) and randinit (7.557.55): a single optimiser step already moves the depth profile measurably away from the random-init shape toward the trained shape; the developmental-arc figure (Figure 2) is the same signal in time-series form, with the ratio against the X0X_{0} embedding rising from ∼12×\sim 12\times to a peak of ∼299×\sim 299\times and settling to ∼206×\sim 206\times during pretraining. The amplification gap is qualitative dynamics evidence (training reduces no-cancellation slack, so the bottom-of-active-spectrum direction propagates with larger leading coefficient), not a predicted scaling, the corollary predicts only the rate-00 statement; the magnitude is empirical.

LN-kernel finding (§4).

Under the centered-covariance protocol, the exact prediction ubotpost=γ−1/‖γ−1‖u_{\mathrm{bot}}^{\mathrm{post}}=\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\| is validated to |cos|≥0.9999|\cos|\geq 0.9999 on all 99 LN models with a post-sequence terminal norm (mean |cos|>0.99999|\cos|>0.99999), spanning next-token CE, DINO-SSL, MAE reconstruction, contrastive-image-text, ImageNet classification, and predictive-video-SSL objectives, with the zero-γ\gamma-coordinate limit applied where relevant. The raw-Gram protocol agrees with centered to |Δ​cos|<0.02|\Delta\cos|<0.02 on 88 of these 99 models; vit-base (ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16) is the exception at |cos|raw=0.54|\cos|_{\mathrm{raw}}=0.54 vs |cos|centered=1.000|\cos|_{\mathrm{centered}}=1.000, traceable to its LN bias having |cos⁡(β,γ−1)|=0.24|\cos(\beta,\gamma^{-1})|=0.24. RMSNorm models sit at |cos|≤0.10|\cos|\leq 0.10 on the γ−1\gamma^{-1} test (centered), the expected no-kernel differential. The uniform-γ\gamma approximation γ−1/‖γ−1‖≈𝟏d/d\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\|\approx\mathbf{1}_{d}/\sqrt{d} holds at |cos|≥0.93|\cos|\geq 0.93 on 66 of 99 LN models and deviates predictably on DINOv2-base (γ\gamma has a slightly-negative coordinate, |cos⁡(γ−1,𝟏d)|=0.54|\cos(\gamma^{-1},\mathbf{1}_{d})|=0.54), DINOv3-ViT-L (γ\gamma has a coordinate pinned to exactly zero, 0.0430.043), and ViT-B/16 (strongly dispersed γ\gamma, 0.0070.007, the most extreme case); on these models the measured cosine matches cos⁡(γ−1,𝟏d)\cos(\gamma^{-1},\mathbf{1}_{d}) to 3 decimals, confirming that the prediction tracks the learned γ−1\gamma^{-1} rather than the projector kernel 𝟏d\mathbf{1}_{d}. Measuring the same coherence at the block-output hook (pre-final-normalization) gives a training-dynamics quantity rather than the algebraic kernel: ≥0.955\geq 0.955 on LN++CE Pythia models, 0.010.01–0.060.06 on LN++SSL vision transformers, reflecting that CE training independently drives 𝟏d\mathbf{1}_{d} toward low-variance directions while SSL training does not. The kernel prediction is about LN’s forward map and must be read at the hook where LN executes.

A.5.1 Pretraining-trajectory developmental arc at LLM scale (Pythia-1b revisions)

To test whether Corollary 58’s residual-stream no-depth-decay and Proposition 63’s LN-kernel claim hold across an actual large-scale pretraining trajectory, we run the σmin\sigma_{\min} fingerprint on 88 published Pythia-1b pretraining checkpoints (step1, step1000, step5000, step10000, step25000, step50000, step100000, main == step 143,000143{,}000) loaded directly from the EleutherAI HuggingFace revisions. Each revision is a fresh forward pass over the WikiText-103 calibration corpus, then fp64 covariance SVD per block.

Findings.

The two predictions hold cross-trajectory, not only at the mature checkpoint.

  • •

    Residual-stream no-depth-decay (Corollary 58). σmin​(Xℓ)/σmin​(X0)≥1\sigma_{\min}(X_{\ell})/\sigma_{\min}(X_{0})\geq 1 on every block on every revision. The ratio is 12×12\times at step1 (network is at untrained initialisation; the residual skip already preserves the input σmin\sigma_{\min} signal, the corollary’s ≥1\geq 1 prediction, at this checkpoint, with the ratio above 11 reflecting per-block LN normalization that lifts low-variance directions; the ≥1\geq 1 ratio is the corollary’s prediction, the specific 12×12\times amplitude is empirical and not predicted), rises to ∼33×\sim 33\times by step1000, grows to a peak of ∼299×\sim 299\times around step50000, and settles to ∼206×\sim 206\times at the mature checkpoint. The corollary’s prediction, that the residual stream bypasses the block operator’s algebraic kernel, so rate-00 preservation holds even as every block degrades σmin\sigma_{\min}, holds at every pretraining step, not as an emergent property of the final loss minimum.

  • •

    LN-kernel prediction (Proposition 63). |cos⁡(ubot,γ−1)|∈[0.998,1.000]|\cos(u_{\mathrm{bot}},\gamma^{-1})|\in[0.998,1.000] on all 88 revisions. The prediction is exact (1.0001.000) at step1 and step1000 because γ\gamma is still at (or near) initialisation γ≡1\gamma\equiv 1, so γ−1/‖γ−1‖=𝟏d/d\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\|=\mathbf{1}_{d}/\sqrt{d} and both columns agree. As γ\gamma trains and disperses, the uniform-γ\gamma cosine |cos⁡(ubot,𝟏d/d)||\cos(u_{\mathrm{bot}},\mathbf{1}_{d}/\sqrt{d})| decays monotonically to 0.9910.991 while the exact prediction |cos⁡(ubot,γ−1)||\cos(u_{\mathrm{bot}},\gamma^{-1})| stays pinned at ≥0.998\geq 0.998. The gap between the two curves in Figure 2(d) is a direct quantitative validation of Proposition 63’s γ\gamma-dependence: the kernel is a property of the learned γ\gamma at every checkpoint, not the initialisation γ\gamma.

The released code accepts any HuggingFace revision tag directly, so the same fingerprint can be re-run at any pretraining checkpoint of any Pythia-like model. main is the EleutherAI consolidated upload of step 143,000143{,}000 and serves as the mature checkpoint.

ViT FFN fine-tuning trajectory test.

The pretrained-fingerprint experiments above are static observations on released checkpoints; they do not exercise the non-cancellation hypothesis (Remark 59) dynamically. To test the corollary along an actual training trajectory we fine-tune DINOv2-base on ImageNet-1k (first-100 classes, ∼128\sim 128k train images) for 2020 epochs across 55 seeds, training only the FFN sub-layers (mlp.fc1, mlp.fc2) of all 1212 blocks while freezing the patch embedding, attention, all LayerNorms, LayerScale, the terminal norm, and the classifier head. We measure σmin​(Xℓ)/σmin​(X0)\sigma_{\min}(X_{\ell})/\sigma_{\min}(X_{0}) at every block at every epoch on a fixed 320320-image held-out calibration batch (drawn from ImageNet-1k validation classes 900900–999999, disjoint from the training distribution; centered-covariance protocol, n/d=107.0n/d=107.0 exceeding the canonical n/d≥100n/d\geq 100 measurement threshold).

Remark 8 (Validation under FFN fine-tuning).

Across 1,2601{,}260 measurement points (55 seeds ×\times 2121 epochs ×\times 1212 blocks) the minimum observed ratio is 109.58109.58, attained at the pre-training snapshot at the shallowest block, the natural geometric minimum, not a fine-tuning-induced inversion. The mean ratio at depth ℓ=1\ell=1 across seeds rises monotonically from 109.58109.58 at epoch 00 to 201.6±2.5201.6\pm 2.5 at epoch 2020, with no local decrease at any epoch on any seed (Figure 5). Cross-seed agreement is tight (final ‖fc1‖\|\mathrm{fc}_{1}\| mean 33.12±0.00733.12\pm 0.007; final val accuracy 0.785±0.0020.785\pm 0.002). The non-cancellation hypothesis behind Corollary 58 is therefore satisfied with substantial margin throughout this trajectory: as the FFN sub-layers move (‖fc1‖\|\mathrm{fc}_{1}\| grows by ∼36%\sim 36\% over training), the residual stream’s depth-invariance margin expands rather than degrading, indicating that gradient-based FFN fine-tuning does not drive the residual branch into a sign-flipped configuration that would partially cancel the identity skip in the bottom singular direction.

A.6 Schur-ratio diagnostic: full 1111-model cross-architecture sweep

The bridge framework’s closed-form Schur constant ( Shirodkar, 2026, Lem. 18) pins down the leading prefactor of the activation-Gram Schur complement and yields a width-only invariant

R⁡(h):=λmin​(Aℓ)(Aℓ)u,u,Aℓ=Xℓ⊤​Xℓ/N,R(h)\;:=\;\frac{\lambda_{\min}(A_{\ell})}{(A_{\ell})_{u,\,u}},\qquad A_{\ell}=X_{\ell}^{\top}X_{\ell}/N,

to be evaluated along the framework-predicted dead direction uu. For the input to a LayerNorm-fed Linear layer (the QKV / MLP-up-projection sites of any pre-norm transformer), the LN-kernel proposition predicts u=γ−1/‖γ−1‖u=\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\|, with R⁡(h)→1R(h)\to 1 at the asymptotic limit. We test this on an 1111-model cross-architecture sweep (55 LayerNorm Pythia sizes spanning h∈{512,…,2560}h\in\{512,\ldots,2560\} plus 66 RMSNorm models: Qwen2.52.5-0.50.5B, LLaMA-22-77B, Gemma 22-22B, Gemma 33-11B/44B, Gemma 44-E44B; partial overlap with the 1414-model fingerprint set of §4). Calibration corpus: 128128 sequences ×\times 10241024 positions =N=131,072=N=131{,}072 tokens drawn from a cascading loader (WikiText-103103 validation split when locally cached, falling back to allenai/c4 validation shards otherwise; both corpora give Schur readings agreeing to |Δγ|<0.01|\Delta_{\gamma}|<0.01 on the 44 models we ran on both). The token budget is chosen to push finite-NN Marchenko–Pastur drift below the algebraic signal at the largest Pythia widths. Activations captured at the QKV input of every transformer block; per-block Aℓ=Xℓ⊤​Xℓ/NA_{\ell}=X_{\ell}^{\top}X_{\ell}/N in fp6464, then R⁡(h)R(h) along u=γ−1/‖γ−1‖u=\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\| read from each block’s pre-attention LN affine. Each Pythia LayerNorm model runs across 55 random-init seeds {42,142,242,342,442}\{42,142,242,342,442\} (torch.manual_seed(seed), AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(cfg)); the trained-checkpoint reading is from the released weights. RMSNorm models, where no algebraic baseline exists to test, run at single-seed 4242 only.

Noise-floor recovery for blocks where both λmin​(Aℓ)\lambda_{\min}(A_{\ell}) and (Aℓ)u,u(A_{\ell})_{u,u} sit at the fp6464 cov floor. The framework predicts λmin​(Aℓ)\lambda_{\min}(A_{\ell}) along γ−1\gamma^{-1} approaches zero algebraically at random init (LN’s kernel direction). Under fp6464 covariance accumulation a near-zero eigenvalue can return as a small negative number from accumulator-order rounding. When this happens both λmin​(Aℓ)\lambda_{\min}(A_{\ell}) and (Aℓ)u,u(A_{\ell})_{u,u} sit at the same numerical floor with the same sign and magnitudes below 10−410^{-4}; we treat the pair as evidence for the algebraic prediction and recover Δγ=1−|λmin​(Aℓ)|/|(Aℓ)u,u|\Delta_{\gamma}=1-|\lambda_{\min}(A_{\ell})|/|(A_{\ell})_{u,u}|. With this recovery applied, the per-block measurement covers all sites at every seed; without it, sites where the prediction holds tightest are excluded by the fp6464 floor and the pooled summary is biased upward. Per-model Δγ\Delta_{\gamma} in Tab. 1 is the pooled median across all (seed, block) measurements with this recovery applied.

The Pythia random-init Schur ratio holds within numerical floor of the algebraic prediction at h≥768h\geq 768. The pooled-median Δγ\Delta_{\gamma} across 55 seeds and all attention sites reads −0.025-0.025 to −0.010-0.010 for Pythia 160160M, 410410M, 11B, and 2.82.8B, with IQRs entirely within [−0.05,+0.01][-0.05,+0.01] (Tab. 1). Negative pooled medians occur because at the noise floor |λmin​(Aℓ)||\lambda_{\min}(A_{\ell})| fluctuates around |(Aℓ)u,u||(A_{\ell})_{u,u}| with random sign of the difference; the IQR captures the noise band. Pythia-7070M (h=512h{=}512, 66 blocks) reads pooled median +0.232+0.232 with IQR [+0.08,+0.30][+0.08,+0.30]: the small block count and wider eigengap at this size give a measurable non-zero Δγ\Delta_{\gamma} that sits above the noise floor. The framework’s prediction R⁡(γ−1)→1R(\gamma^{-1})\to 1 at random init is met to numerical precision for h≥768h\geq 768 and within ∼0.2\sim\!0.2 at h=512h{=}512.

Training opens dead directions below the LN-kernel algebraic baseline. At every Pythia checkpoint at the trained weights, Δγ​(h)≥0.999\Delta_{\gamma}(h)\geq 0.999 across all sizes (Tab. 1); R⁡(h)R(h) along the framework-predicted direction has collapsed to near-zero. At trained Pythia-7070M block 00 on the QKV input, λmin​(A)=1.96×10−3\lambda_{\min}(A)=1.96\times 10^{-3} while (A)γ−1,γ−1=2.40(A)_{\gamma^{-1},\gamma^{-1}}=2.40: the bottom eigenvector of AA has eigenvalue 1.2×103×1.2\times 10^{3}\times smaller than the projection along γ−1/‖γ−1‖\gamma^{-1}/\|\gamma^{-1}\|. The algebraic-kernel direction is no longer the deepest dead direction; training has produced additional dead directions below the architectural-algebraic baseline. The trained-vs-random gap in Δγ\Delta_{\gamma} is a forward-pass-only diagnostic of how much singular structure has accumulated below the algebraic null on a given checkpoint.

RMSNorm models confirm the no-universal-kernel differential. The five RMSNorm families in the sweep (Qwen2.52.5-0.50.5B, LLaMA-22-77B, Gemma 22/33/44; six models total) have Δγ​(h)≈0.80\Delta_{\gamma}(h)\approx 0.80–0.970.97 at random init, the framework’s R⁡(γ−1)=1R(\gamma^{-1})=1 prediction does not hold at random init, in contrast to the LayerNorm models. Trained checkpoints saturate at Δγ≈0.99\Delta_{\gamma}\approx 0.99–1.001.00, confirming that the γ−1\gamma^{-1} direction is no closer to a kernel of RMSNorm’s forward map than a generic direction. RMSNorm has no orthogonal-to-𝟏\mathbf{1} algebraic constraint ( Shirodkar, 2026, Prop. 63), so γ−1\gamma^{-1} is not a near-null direction of its forward map; the negative companion proposition is the framework’s prediction here, and the data confirm it. The 1111-model sweep therefore separates cleanly along the LN/RMSNorm dichotomy: LayerNorm models permit a clean random-init test of the algebraic null and a clean trained-checkpoint signal of training-induced structure; RMSNorm models do not admit the same baseline because the underlying algebraic constraint is absent.

What the diagnostic enables. The Schur-ratio along the framework’s predicted direction acts as a per-checkpoint, per-block algebraic reference for LayerNorm-equipped models. At random init, R⁡(γ−1)R(\gamma^{-1}) is the algebraic baseline (→1\to 1 to within fp6464 cov noise floor); on the trained checkpoint, the gap Δγtrained−Δγrand\Delta_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{trained}}-\Delta_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{rand}} is a forward-pass-only diagnostic of how much singular structure has accumulated below the algebraic null. No gradient access is required; no optimiser-state hooks. This sharpens the σmin\sigma_{\min} depth-invariance fingerprint of (b) into a per-block, per-checkpoint scalar diagnostic with two endpoints fixed by the framework. Identification of the trained-network’s deepest direction (which is no longer γ−1\gamma^{-1}), its stability across batches, and its correlation with massive-activation features are open follow-on probes.

Mechanism diagnosis on the Gemma σmin\sigma_{\min} anomaly.

The Gemma44-3131B (depth-decreasing) and Gemma44-E44B (intermediate-dip) σmin\sigma_{\min} failures above are the most pronounced empirical signal in the LLM-scale fingerprint. A family discriminator across Gemma 11 through Gemma 44, run under the same protocol as the main table (fp3232 forward, fp6464 cov, bot-kk 3232, n/d≥10n/d\geq 10, referenced against the true input embedding X0X_{0}), localises the failure to the Gemma 44 release: pre-LN Gemma 11 and Peri-LN (Kim et al., 2025) Gemma 22/33 all preserve σmin\sigma_{\min} (Tab. 4), and only Gemma 44 fails. Sharing the Peri-LN block pattern (RMSNorm both before and after the sublayer; Team, 2024a, Tab. 1; Team, 2025) is therefore not sufficient for the failure: Gemma 22/33 use it and pass, and the failure does not track the normalization placement at all, since pre-LN Gemma 11 passes too. Corollary 58’s no-cancellation hypothesis (Rem. 59) requires that the residual-branch contribution not cancel the identity at the bottom-of-active-spectrum direction; on Gemma 44 the residual stream nonetheless loses ∼30×\sim 30\times in σmin\sigma_{\min} at the mid-depth dip. We test five candidate mechanisms by which the no-cancellation hypothesis could fail on Gemma 44.

γpost\gamma_{\mathrm{post}}-kernel formation in the post-norm delta (rejected). The hypothesis is that the post-norm RMSNorm’s effective scale γposteff=1+weight\gamma_{\mathrm{post}}^{\mathrm{eff}}=1+\mathrm{weight} (Gemma’s (1+γ)(1+\gamma) reparameterisation, Team, 2026a) develops near-zero coordinates at the affected blocks, creating an algebraic kernel direction analogous to Proposition 63’s LN kernel acting in the post-norm delta. Reading γposteff\gamma_{\mathrm{post}}^{\mathrm{eff}} off the affine parameter at all four norm positions per block of Gemma44-3131B (no forward pass, safetensors-only): no coordinate satisfies |γposteff|min<0.1⋅|γposteff|¯|\gamma_{\mathrm{post}}^{\mathrm{eff}}|_{\min}<0.1\cdot\overline{|\gamma_{\mathrm{post}}^{\mathrm{eff}}|} at any block; concentration ratio max⁡(γ)/|γ|¯\max(\gamma)/\overline{|\gamma|} is mild (median 1.171.17 in mid-section blocks 99–5555, 1.301.30 at end blocks); the Spearman correlation between post​_​mlp\mathrm{post\_mlp} concentration and log⁡σmin​(Xℓ+1)/σmin​(X0)\log\sigma_{\min}(X_{\ell+1})/\sigma_{\min}(X_{0}) is +0.74+0.74, the opposite sign of the kernel-formation prediction. The hypothesis is rejected for Gemma44-3131B; Proposition 63 predicts no γ\gamma-derived universal kernel direction for RMSNorm, consistent with this.

Per-block residual-vs-delta principal-angle alignment (rejected on both Gemma44 checkpoints with different fingerprints). The hypothesis is that the trained network has structurally aligned the bottom-kk subspace of XℓX_{\ell} with a high-magnitude subspace of the post-norm delta DℓD_{\ell} at the affected blocks, with anti-correlated cross-row inner products on the aligned direction. Test: a 100×2048100\times 2048 C44 calibration forward, hooking the residual stream and per-block deltas at architecture-aware positions (post​_​attention​_​layernorm\mathrm{post\_attention\_layernorm} and post​_​feedforward​_​layernorm\mathrm{post\_feedforward\_layernorm} outputs for Gemma; attention.dense\mathrm{attention.dense} and mlp.dense​_​4​h​_​to​_​h\mathrm{mlp.dense\_4h\_to\_h} for Pythia GPT-NeoX; self​_​attn.o​_​proj\mathrm{self\_attn.o\_proj} and mlp.down​_​proj\mathrm{mlp.down\_proj} for Qwen). Centred covariance accumulated in fp6464; bottom-k=8k=8 subspaces via torch.linalg.eigh on CPU. Per-model summary in Tab. 3. Gemma44-E44B has elevated alignment (max mean cos=0.77\cos=0.77) but Spearman(log⁡r,cos¯)=+0.25(\log r,\overline{\cos})=+0.25, alignment goes up with σmin\sigma_{\min}, the opposite of the cancellation-hypothesis sign. Gemma44-3131B has universally low alignment (max mean cos=0.46\cos=0.46, never crossing the 0.60.6 cancellation-pathology threshold); the Spearman has the cancellation sign (−0.53-0.53), but the most-collapsed block (5252, ratio 0.0200.020) has mean cos=0.12\cos=0.12, among the lowest alignments. The negative correlation is driven by moderate-alignment middle blocks, not by the deeply-collapsed end. The two checkpoints exhibit different per-block alignment fingerprints yet both show the σmin\sigma_{\min} collapse, ruling out any fixed per-block alignment mechanism that would scale with architecture.

Sandwich-norm / Peri-LN architectural pattern as cause (rejected). The hypothesis is that the post-norm wrapping of the sublayer output is the architectural feature that produces σmin\sigma_{\min} collapse. Test: run the residual-stream σmin\sigma_{\min} fingerprint on the Gemma family, comparing Gemma 11 (Team, 2024b) (pre-LN only, no post-norm wrapping) against Gemma 22/33 (Peri-LN sandwich-norm) and Gemma 44. The ablation is uniquely clean within this family: same author group, same RMSNorm + GeGLU + RoPE + GQA foundation, same training-data lineage; the post-norm wrapping is the architecturally-relevant change between Gemma 11 and Gemma 22. Tab. 4 reports the per-model fingerprint under the corrected fp3232-forward + fp6464-cov + X0X_{0}-reference protocol. Pre-LN Gemma 11-22b/77b and Peri-LN Gemma 22-22b, Gemma 33-11b/44b/1212b all preserve σmin\sigma_{\min} at every block (min ratio ≥1.8\geq 1.8, output 9.99.9–632×632\times); only the Gemma 44 release fails. The failure does not track the normalization placement: pre-LN Gemma 11 and Peri-LN Gemma 22/33 all pass, and the failure appears only in the Gemma 44 release, so the post-norm wrapping is not sufficient to produce it. The depth-cumulative version of the hypothesis (compression scaling with LL) is independently rejected by Gemma 33-1212b at L=48L=48, the deepest non-Gemma-4 model in the set, achieving 612×612\times σmin\sigma_{\min} growth from the embedding to its output.

Centred-cov estimator artefact via sink-token / register-token bias (rejected). The hypothesis is that RMSNorm-equipped models concentrate massive activations at register / BOS tokens (Sun et al., 2024), and the centred-covariance estimator’s per-coordinate mean subtraction is overwhelmed by a small fraction of dominant tokens, with the bottom-of-spectrum reading off the off-cluster minority’s spread rather than the residual stream’s geometric rank. Test: a single forward pass on Gemma44-E44B with six covariance estimators streamed in parallel per block, centred (baseline), sink-excised (per-chunk top-1%1\% by ‖X‖\|X\| removed), median-anchored (per-coordinate per-chunk median subtracted instead of mean), and three position-stratified streams (BOS-only, first-non-BOS, other-positions ≥2\geq 2). The collapse persists across the four estimators with well-defined σmin\sigma_{\min}: minimum ratio 0.0690.069 (centred), 0.0720.072 (sink-excised), 0.0690.069 (median-anchored), 0.0690.069 (other-positions); frac≥1\geq 1 = 0.500.50 in all four. Removing the top 1%1\% of tokens by ‖X‖\|X\| does not flatten the collapse; the median-anchored estimator agrees with centred to three significant figures; the bulk-position stream is identical to centred.

Post-pretraining stage as source (rejected). All five Gemma 44 variants fail against X0X_{0} at the canonical protocol (Tab. 4): the three base (pretrained) checkpoints E2B, E4B, 3131B and the two instruct checkpoints E2B-it, E4B-it. The base checkpoints fail before any instruct / RLHF / distillation post-training, so the failure originates in pretraining itself. Instruct-tuning does not remove it; the instruct variants fail at least as pervasively as their base counterparts (E2B-it 35/3535/35 blocks below X0X_{0} against E2B’s 27/3527/35; E4B-it 42/4242/42 against E4B’s 24/4224/42).

The failure is universal across the Gemma 44 release at every tested size (55B E2B, 88B E4B, 3232B 3131B) and in both base and instruct form, with min ratio 0.0050.005–0.0320.032. The recovery pattern varies: E4B (base) dips and recovers to 1.08×1.08\times by the output (intermediate-dip), while E2B, 3131B, and both instruct variants end below X0X_{0} (depth-decreasing). Across the family the verdict is unambiguous: only the Gemma 44 release fails, while pre-LN Gemma 11 (22b, 77b) and Peri-LN Gemma 22/33 all pass at L=−48L=18\!-\!48.

Where the collapse sits: the MLP sub-layer (positive localization). The sub-layer-resolved fingerprint taps σmin\sigma_{\min} at the block input, after the attention sub-layer, and at the block output, localizing each σmin\sigma_{\min} drop to attention (input→\tomid) or MLP (mid→\tooutput). In both failing Gemma 44 checkpoints the drops concentrate on the MLP: 28/4228/42 blocks lower σmin\sigma_{\min} across the MLP on E4B against 2/422/42 across attention, and 40/6040/60 against 6/606/60 on 3131B (Tab. 4, MLP-locus column). At the minimum-ratio block the MLP sub-layer collapses the effective rank under a massive-activation write (E4B block 2323: eff-rank 47→1647\to 16, σmax≈1.2×104\sigma_{\max}\approx 1.2\times 10^{4}; 3131B block 5353: 27→1527\to 15, σmax≈1.7×104\sigma_{\max}\approx 1.7\times 10^{4}). The MLP write that concentrates residual-stream variance into a few outlier directions (Sun et al., 2024) cancels variance along the pre-existing bottom direction, the no-cancellation hypothesis (Rem. 59) failing locally at an MLP sub-layer. The same MLP-driven local cancellation appears sub-threshold in the passing releases (the MLP-locus counts are nonzero on Gemma 11/22/33), but there it stays above X0X_{0}; the Gemma 44 recipe is the regime where it goes pervasively below.

Surviving candidates. With post-pretraining ruled out, two candidates remain for the cause; the first (recipe difference) is not separately tested, the second (calibration distribution) we resolve directly below:

  1. 1.

    Pretraining-recipe difference between Gemma 44 and Gemma 22/33. Recipe and architectural variables drift jointly across Gemma versions: logit soft-capping (Gemma 22 only), QK-norm (Gemma 33/44), multimodal pretraining (Gemma 44), distillation schedules, sliding-window attention parameters, GQA head-group ratios, tied-embedding scaling factors, rotary base values. The failure could be driven by any subset that incidentally tracks the dichotomy; we have directly ruled out only the post-norm wrapping and the post-pretraining stage. Discriminator: per-feature ablation across the family, requires inspecting each architectural / training-recipe variable for its fail/pass alignment.

  2. 2.

    Calibration-distribution interaction. The fingerprint protocol uses text-only C44; Gemma 44 is multimodal and its residual stream geometry on text-only calibration may be unrepresentative of its in-domain regime. We carry out this discriminator below: multimodal recalibration resolves the dichotomy (E4B distribution-relative, 3131B intrinsic).

Calibration-distribution interaction: tested. Gemma 44 is encoder-free natively multimodal: the vision tower, and on E4B an audio tower, feed soft tokens directly into the shared backbone, so text-only calibration leaves those soft-token subspaces dormant. We re-run the σmin\sigma_{\min} fingerprint with image and image++audio calibration (ImageNet-11k validation images and LibriSpeech audio through the model’s processor, the same fp3232-forward ++ fp6464-cov observable). The two checkpoints separate (Tab. 5). On the tri-modal E4B the dip dissolves as modalities are added: output σmin\sigma_{\min} rises from 6.16.1 under image to 9.99.9 under image++audio, the worst-block σmin\sigma_{\min} rises with it, and re-projecting the text-only bottom singular direction onto the image++audio stream lifts it 2.22.2–8.7×8.7\times at depth (cosine 0.970.97 with the image++audio bottom at the dip block). The text-only minimum direction is the activated multimodal subspace, so E4B’s dip is a distribution-relative dead direction and the model carries no intrinsic dead direction. On the bi-modal 3131B (vision++text, with no audio tower: audio_config null, zero audio weights) image calibration lifts the text-only direction by 2.82.8–4.9×4.9\times, yet a residual near-dead direction remains at block 5252. It holds across sample budget (σmin=0.013\sigma_{\min}=0.013 at n/d≈10n/d\approx 10, 0.0200.020 at n/d≈20n/d\approx 20) and sits 7.9×7.9\times above the fp3232 measurement floor at full rank, identifying a genuine intrinsic near-dead direction under 3131B’s full available distribution.

Measurement floor. σmin\sigma_{\min} is resolved only down to the fp3232 forward floor σmaxraw⋅ε32\sigma_{\max}^{\mathrm{raw}}\cdot\varepsilon_{32} with ε32≈1.2×10−7\varepsilon_{32}\approx 1.2\times 10^{-7}: fp3232 roundoff acts on the raw massive activations, and the fp6464 covariance corrects accumulation order without recovering signal beneath it. A truly dead direction reads at this floor with active rank r0r_{0} below full; 3131B’s residual reads 7.9×7.9\times above it at full rank (r0=5376r_{0}=5376), placing it clear of the floor as resolved signal. Probing beneath the floor would need an fp6464 forward, which trips Gemma’s rotary-embedding fp3232 assertion and exceeds memory at 3131B scale.

What the diagnosis establishes. The σmin\sigma_{\min} failure is empirically dissociated from five named mechanisms: γpost\gamma_{\mathrm{post}}-derived kernel formation; per-block residual-delta principal-angle cancellation; the Peri-LN sandwich-norm architectural pattern itself; centred-cov sink-token estimator bias; and post-pretraining stage as source. The family discriminator isolates it to the Gemma 44 release: pre-LN Gemma 11 and Peri-LN Gemma 22/33 all pass against X0X_{0}, so the failure is dissociated from the normalisation placement, and the sub-layer fingerprint localises it to the MLP. Multimodal recalibration resolves the calibration-distribution candidate: E4B’s text-only dip is a distribution-relative dead direction that dissolves under its full text++image++audio distribution, while 3131B retains a genuine intrinsic near-dead direction above the fp3232 measurement floor; the recipe-difference candidate is not separately tested. Corollary 58 holds cleanly on Pythia-11B, Qwen3.53.5-44B, Gemma 11-22b/77b, Gemma 22-22b, Gemma 33-11b/44b/1212b and the broader 12/1412/14-pass cross-architecture set; its no-cancellation hypothesis (Rem. 59) is checkpoint-failable, with the failure on the Gemma 44 release characterised at both re-run sizes (E4B recovers to the output, 3131B does not) and localised to the MLP sub-layer.

A.7 Cross-architecture feasibility (vision-class widths)

The cost-information trade-off characterised in §4(a) shifts at smaller architecture widths. At vision-transformer scale (h≤1024h\leq 1024), the per-layer λmin​(Gℓ)\lambda_{\min}(G_{\ell}) requirement of n≥100​hn\geq 100h samples is ≤102,400\leq 102{,}400 samples per layer, which at batch size 128128 is ≤800\leq 800 FBPs per layer, real-time per checkpoint on a single GPU. All four observables therefore operate at the same always-on cadence on vision-class architectures, in contrast to the LLM regime where the full-spectrum λmin​(G)\lambda_{\min}(G) measurement shifts to offline cadence owing to cubic scaling in hh. The six LN-based vision transformers reported in Table 2 (h∈{384,768,1024}h\in\{384,768,1024\}, 1212–2424 blocks) have σmin\sigma_{\min} fingerprint wall-clock under 11 s per model on a single 3090; full-spectrum λmin​(G)\lambda_{\min}(G) eigendecomposition remains feasible at this width. The 1414-model set already spans LN/RMSNorm ×\times language-CE / image-SSL / contrastive / predictive-SSL combinations (§A.5); diffusion UNets and audio encoders are natural targets for the same fingerprint protocol that we have not yet exercised.

A.8 Compute and reproducibility

All experiments run on a single workstation: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 9955WX (16c/32t), 256 GB DDR5 ECC, 4×4\times NVIDIA RTX 3090 (24 GB). Total compute to reproduce the experiments reported in this paper: ∼\sim1717 GPU-hours, dominated by the Gemma σmin\sigma_{\min} mechanism diagnostic across the Gemma 11/22/33/44 family (fp6464 cov on 55+ models with multiple variants).

The experiments reported in the body and bound appendix are: the LLM scale-pipeline (1414-model σmin\sigma_{\min} fingerprint sweep, fp3232/fp6464 cov by σmax\sigma_{\max} regime; §A.5); the Gemma σmin\sigma_{\min} mechanism diagnostic across the Gemma 11/22/33/44 family with base/instruct contrast, size-scaling sweep, residual-stream principal-angle and centered-vs.-sink-excised variants (§A.6); the Schur-ratio R⁡(h)R(h) cross-model sweep on 1111 pretrained models (Pythia LayerNorm sizes run at 55 random-init seeds and two token budgets N∈{32,768,131,072}N\in\{32{,}768,131{,}072\} with noise-floor recovery; §4, §A.6); and the ViT FFN fine-tuning trajectory test (55 seeds DINOv22-base on ImageNet-1k first-100; §A.5).

Per-experiment wall-clock and GPU usage is recorded in each result JSON’s metadata block (run_started_at, gpu_model, cuda_visible_devices, plus driver-specific timing fields where relevant); aggregate per-sweep timing is reproducible from the launcher logs under the corresponding results/ directory. The trajectory-rate validation experiments (parametric autoencoder rate-fits, canonical-bridge ablations, L=4L{=}4 noisy-bridge rate-chain validation, Barak / Nanda grokking sweeps, the Aoyagi closed-form RLCT anchor) are out of scope for this paper.

Code release.

The experiment scripts, the σmin\sigma_{\min} core library, scale-pipeline tooling, Schur-ratio probe, Gemma-family diagnostic scripts, result JSONs, and figure-generation scripts will be released publicly on GitHub under an open-source license; in the interim they are available from the authors on request.

Per-experiment seed lists and exact hyperparameters are documented in each script’s header.

Reproducibility audit.

Every numerical claim in the paper is anchored to a specific JSON via a % TRANSCRIBED FROM: header comment in the originating chunk. A canonical audit script verifies, in one command, that every cited path resolves on disk, every \includegraphics target is present, and headline numbers (|cos||\cos| on the 99 LN models and 55 RMSNorm models, σmin\sigma_{\min} depth-invariance pass-rate with documented exceptions, the Schur-ratio Δγ\Delta_{\gamma} random-init vs trained gap on the Pythia size sweep, and the Gemma family ablation pattern) reproduce within tolerance from their cited JSONs:

python scripts/audit/verify_paper.py

The script also runs as a pre-build gate (empirical_ln_kernel/src/build.sh invokes verify_paper.py --paths before compiling). Single-claim mode (--claim NAME) re-runs one check; --paths mode runs the path-and-figure existence audit only (<1<1 s). Exit status is 0 on full pass; non-zero on any drift or missing path.

Appendix B Empirical compendium

This appendix collects extended empirical results that are referenced but not fully reported in the main paper or the bound submission appendix. The bound submission appendix (§A) contains tables and statistics for stated experiments; this appendix carries the per-layer rate structure empirical validation at LLM scale, the κ\kappa-stability measurement protocol description, and the Adam non-equivariance factorial.

B.1 Per-layer rate structure: empirical validation at LLM scale

The rate formula kℓ=2​(L−ℓ)k_{\ell}=2(L-\ell) predicts shallow layers have greater dead-direction depth (larger kℓk_{\ell}) than deep layers. To test whether this per-layer structure empirically holds at LLM scale beyond parametric probes, we compare three per-layer projection-rank allocations on TinyLlama-1.11.1B (L=22L{=}22 blocks, h=2048h{=}2048):

  • •

    Uniform: kℓ=Ktotal/Lk_{\ell}=K_{\mathrm{total}}/L (all layers equal).

  • •

    Theorem: kℓ∝(L−ℓ)k_{\ell}\propto(L-\ell) (shallow more, deep less).

  • •

    Reverse (control): kℓ∝ℓk_{\ell}\propto\ell (opposite).

We sweep total budget Ktotal/(L⋅h)K_{\mathrm{total}}/(L\cdot h) from 5%5\% to 25%25\% and report WikiText-103 perplexity and PIQA zero-shot accuracy. This is a theorem-structure validation, not a compression method: the goal here is to test whether the per-layer allocation predicted by Theorem 21 measurably manifests in pretrained-model behaviour, not to advocate any practical compression recipe.

We sweep 55 total compression budgets (5%5\%, 10%10\%, 15%15\%, 20%20\%, 25%25\% of L⋅hmodelL\cdot h_{\mathrm{model}}) on TinyLlama-1.11.1B (Figure 7).

Finding.

The theorem’s per-layer structure empirically manifests at LLM scale: the theorem allocation preserves perplexity better than uniform or reverse in the 55–20%20\% budget range (up to 2020 percentage-point ppl advantage; Figure 7A). This is outside cross-seed noise and is consistent with the rate formula’s prediction kℓ=2​(L−ℓ)k_{\ell}=2(L-\ell), extending the parametric validation of Shirodkar (2026)to a real pretrained model.

PIQA task accuracy does not follow this ordering (Figure 7B): the theorem allocation is actually worse than uniform at budgets ≥10%\geq 10\%. The theorem formula is a statement about loss-function dynamics near singular minima, not about which directions carry task-specific semantics; the per-layer rate structure manifesting on perplexity but not on PIQA accuracy is exactly the predicted behaviour, not a contradiction.

B.2 Measurement Protocol: Sample Requirements for Stable κ\kappa

The condition number κ⁡(Gℓ)=λmax/λmin\kappa(G_{\ell})=\lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min} is sensitive to the accuracy of the smallest eigenvalue estimate. For a d×dd\times d sample covariance estimated from nn samples, the Marchenko–Pastur law predicts that λmin\lambda_{\min} is biased downward by approximately (1−d/n)2(1-\sqrt{d/n})^{2}. When n/d≈1n/d\approx 1, this bias is severe and κ\kappa becomes dominated by estimation noise.

We verified this empirically by measuring the same frozen model 10 times with different random data subsets at three sample counts:

Samples (nn) n/dn/d Meas. CV (layer4, d=512d{=}512)
1,280 (nbatches=10n_{\mathrm{batches}}{=}10) 2.5 110%110\%
6,400 (nbatches=50n_{\mathrm{batches}}{=}50) 12.5 66%66\%
50,000 (full dataset) 97.7 <1%{<}1\%

At n/d=2.5n/d=2.5, the measurement CV exceeds 100%, so the estimate is pure noise. At n/d≈100n/d\approx 100, repeated measurements give identical results (CV <1%{<}1\%). This finding has a critical implication: prior empirical work using small KFAC batches (nbatches=5n_{\mathrm{batches}}=5–1010) on architectures with large output channels (d≥256d\geq 256) may be unreliable.

Auto-scaling.

Our implementation inspects the model to find dmaxd_{\max} (the largest output channel count across all tracked layers), then computes nbatches=⌈100⋅dmax/batch_size⌉n_{\mathrm{batches}}=\lceil 100\cdot d_{\max}/\text{batch\_size}\rceil. When this exceeds the dataset size, the full dataset is used. For CIFAR-100 (50K samples): WRN-28-2 (dmax=64d_{\max}=64) uses 50 batches; ResNet-18 and ViT-Small (dmax=512d_{\max}=512) use the full dataset.

Measurement isolation.

The KFAC measurement must not consume the training DataLoader’s shuffle RNG, as this would change the training trajectory and produce different models depending on the measurement schedule. We use a separate non-shuffled DataLoader for all measurements, ensuring complete isolation between monitoring and training.

Position in the four-tier observable hierarchy.

The n/d≥100n/d\geq 100 sample budget analyzed here is the gating constraint for the periodic-tier λmin​(Gℓ)\lambda_{\min}(G_{\ell}) observable. The other three tiers have different cost-vs-information trade-offs and avoid this constraint to varying degrees: the real-time tier σmin​(Xℓ)\sigma_{\min}(X_{\ell}) on the residual stream (Corollary 58) is forward-pass-only and has no n/dn/d requirement (a single forward pass on NN tokens with N≥hN\geq h yields the singular spectrum directly); the checkpoint tier u⊤​G​uu^{\top}Gu at a fixed direction is a single backward pass on demand and is precision-limited rather than sample-limited; the offline tier full-Fisher Lanczos partial decomposition trades much higher cost for the bottom eigenstructure. For real-time monitoring at large scale, σmin​(Xℓ)\sigma_{\min}(X_{\ell}) is preferred over κ⁡(Gℓ)\kappa(G_{\ell}) specifically because the activation-side observable avoids the n/dn/d sample-budget constraint analyzed here.

Depth-dependence of the n/dn/d requirement.

A bootstrap calibration on a representative trajectory at D=100D{=}100 shows the n/d≥100n/d{\geq}100 rule is a useful default at well-conditioned checkpoints (matching the table above) but tightens as σmin\sigma_{\min} descends. At early checkpoints (σmin\sigma_{\min} within ∼1\sim 1 OOM of σmax\sigma_{\max}) the empirical CV(λmin+\lambda_{\min}^{+}) is ≤0.13\leq 0.13 at n/d=50n/d{=}50 and ≤0.015\leq 0.015 at n/d=100n/d{=}100, consistent with the table; at deep singular checkpoints (σmin\sigma_{\min} several OOM below σmax\sigma_{\max}) even n/d=100n/d{=}100 retains CV≈1\mathrm{CV}\approx 1 on λmin+​(G)\lambda_{\min}^{+}(G), magnitude estimates are no longer recoverable at any feasible nn. The fp-precision floor margin σmin/(σmax​εdtype)\sigma_{\min}/(\sigma_{\max}\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{dtype}}}) is the binding constraint in this regime; below margin ∼1\sim 1, no sample count helps.

Analytical CV bound (perturbation theory).

A testbed-agnostic CV upper bound for an isolated smallest active eigenvalue is given by first-order perturbation theory plus Davis-Kahan: CV⁡(λmin+)≤(1/N)⋅(σmax/σmin)\mathrm{CV}(\lambda_{\min}^{+})\leq(1/\sqrt{N})\cdot(\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}). This bound is typically 55–10×10\times pessimistic on structured GG (gradient Fisher matrices), much tighter than the operator-norm Wishart bound D/N⋅(σmax/σmin)2\sqrt{D/N}\cdot(\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min})^{2} which is 5050–500×500\times pessimistic on the same data. The perturbation bound is therefore the appropriate analytical fallback when no testbed-specific calibration is available; the Wishart bound is the guaranteed-valid worst-case ceiling.

Rank-correlation observables: a separate regime.

The depth-dependent failure of magnitude estimates does not compromise rank-correlation observables (Spearman ρ\rho across checkpoints). The rank order of λmin+​(G)\lambda_{\min}^{+}(G) across a trajectory is preserved even when individual magnitudes have CV∼1\mathrm{CV}\sim 1, because rank correlation depends on monotonic co-movement, not on magnitude reproducibility. For slope fits and any other magnitude-dependent reading, the depth-aware n/dn/d requirement is the correct gate; for ρ\rho-based predictions, it is conservative.

Appendix C Optimiser ×\times loss applicability of the empirical observables

We do not introduce new observables in this paper; we use existing observables from the singular-learning, KFAC, and spectral-monitoring literatures. The formal applicability conditions for the rate predictions are stated in Shirodkar (2026). This appendix is a defensive scope reference: it classifies each observable mentioned in the framework by the optimiser ×\times loss combinations under which it remains a valid signal versus those under which its signal is dominated by the Adam non-equivariance failure mode (Remark 80). The main claims of this paper rely only on the static-observable rows (residual-stream σmin\sigma_{\min}, post-norm centred-cov bottom direction, Schur-ratio R⁡(h)R(h) at the predicted direction): every result is read from a single forward pass with no SGLD chain and no gradient access. The trajectory-rate rows are presented for completeness; they are not tested in this paper.

C.1 Static vs trajectory observable applicability

The framework has two distinct classes of observables, validated under different conditions. Mixing them up is the most common reproducer failure mode.

Static observables

(well-defined at any single checkpoint, no trajectory required):

  • •

    σmin​(Xℓ)\sigma_{\min}(X_{\ell}) at any layer

  • •

    σmax​(Xℓ)\sigma_{\max}(X_{\ell}), effective rank, full activation SVD

  • •

    Bottom-singular-direction coherence with 𝟏d/d\mathbf{1}_{d}/\sqrt{d} (LN models)

  • •

    u⊤​G​uu^{\top}Gu at a fixed direction uu (single backward pass), reading Fisher magnitude but not a rate

  • •

    Expected-Fisher spectrum at a single checkpoint

These are valid for any optimizer, any loss, any architecture. The LLM σmin\sigma_{\min} fingerprint, the LN-kernel finding, and the residual-DAG σmin\sigma_{\min} depth-invariance all live here.

Trajectory-rate observables

(require an actual approach to a singular minimum; rate has meaning only along the trajectory):

  • •

    Power-law slope of u⊤​G​uu^{\top}Gu vs tt (or vs σmin\sigma_{\min}, the scale-free ratio)

  • •

    Power-law slope of λmin​(Gℓ)\lambda_{\min}(G_{\ell}) or λp−1​(Fhpop)\lambda_{p-1}(F_{h}^{\mathrm{pop}}) along training

  • •

    Per-layer rate exponent matching Theorem 21’s 2​(L−ℓ)2(L-\ell) prediction

These are valid only when (a) the optimizer is theorem-compatible (SGD on GG-invariant metrics, or empirically Shampoo full-batch and KFAC++KL-clip full-batch on canonical-bridge testbeds), AND (b) the trajectory actually approaches a singular minimum AND (c) the trajectory is canonical-aligned. This paper does not test trajectory-rate observables; they are reproduced for reference and not validated in this paper.
